drug_class: Farnesoid X Receptor (FXR) Agonist / Bile Acid Derivative
purpose: Obeticholic acid is used to treat a liver disease called primary biliary cholangitis, or PBC, which causes bile to build up and damage your liver over time. It is usually used along with another medication called ursodiol when ursodiol alone is not working well enough. It helps protect your liver from further damage.
how_it_works: Your liver makes bile to help digest food, but in PBC, bile builds up and harms liver cells. Obeticholic acid works by activating a special protein in your liver called FXR, which acts like a switch that tells your body to make less bile and reduce inflammation. Think of it as turning down the production of a substance that is causing harm, giving your liver a chance to recover.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is itching of the skin, which can sometimes be intense. You may also notice tiredness, stomach pain, joint pain, swelling in your belly, rash, dizziness, heart palpitations, or a fever. Some people also experience constipation or an uncomfortable feeling in their stomach.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems, especially if your liver disease is already advanced — so your doctor will monitor your liver closely with regular blood tests. Do not use this medicine if you have a complete blockage of your bile ducts. It can also raise your cholesterol levels, so your doctor will check that too. Tell your doctor right away if your skin or eyes turn yellow, or if your swelling or itching gets much worse. Always take this medicine exactly as prescribed and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth once a day. If your body tolerates it well and your doctor feels you need a stronger effect, the dose may be increased to 10 mg once a day after about 3 months. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on how your liver is doing.
